Subject: Dedicated capacity: autoscaling & queue sizing follow-up

Thanks again for taking the call today — great to meet the Acme team. Quick follow-up / recap and proposed next steps so we can scope Dedicated capacity correctly.

Call highlights (summary):
- Goal: Dedicated capacity for production inference across customer-facing features (chat, product Q&A, and re-ranking pipelines).
- Key workloads: low-latency chat (SLO 200ms p50, 700ms p95), batched nightly re-ranks (~10k queries/hour), embeddings generation for real-time personalization (~150 qps, mostly async).
- Current constraints: On-prem data residency for some data, requirement for predictable tail latency, and ability to scale up for marketing spikes.

Action items we discussed (what we need from you):
1) Traffic profile: per-route QPS, typical and peak concurrency, percentiles for request sizes (prompt/token lengths). If you can share the sample CSV we can baseline autoscaler knobs.
2) SLOs: confirm p50/p95/p99 targets per route and acceptable error budget for fallbacks.
3) Embeddings: expected queries/sec and whether embeddings are synchronous on request path or done offline for re-rankers.
4) Auth & SDK: preferred auth (API keys vs mTLS+OIDC); any internal SDK constraints.
5) Routing/tenancy: do you want per-customer queues/pools or a shared multi-tenant pool with per-route priorities?

Proposed technical next step: schedule a 60-min deep-dive with Aditya and Dev to go over the proposed multipool architecture (attached) and sizing assumptions. If you can upload the traffic sample (or allow us to use the one you mentioned), Aditya will run a quick sim to estimate node counts and queue depths.

Attachments: proposed_multipool_arch.png (diagram), acme_dedicated_requirements_v2.pdf (notes).

Proposed times: I can do Tue/Wed morning PST — please let me know what works and I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. This looks good. A couple quick data points while we pull the full CSV:

- Chat (prod): avg 40 qps, peak 220 qps during promo spikes; typical concurrency per session ~1.2 active requests; median prompt length ~80 tokens; 95th ~420 tokens.
- Re-ranker (near-real-time): average 3 qps per shard, bursts up to 50 qps for batch jobs (we currently fan-out to multiple shards).
- Embeddings: ~150 qps, mostly synchronous in our recommendation service (95% paths expect <300ms additional latency).

We prefer API keys for now, but ops is open to mTLS if you recommend it for private deployment.

Two questions for your team:
1) For per-customer isolation, can we get autoscaling boundaries per pool so we don’t starve other customers during a spike?
2) How does Redwood handle queue backpressure — will requests block client threads or return a retryable error? We prefer soft queuing with retryable 429s and server-side backpressure to avoid client timeouts.

I attached a quick traffic sample export (acme_traffic_sample.csv). Let us know if you need more detail.

—Alex

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: autoscaling & queue sizing follow-up

Thanks Alex — good numbers to start with. I reviewed the diagram Marissa attached and the sample CSV; below are concrete recommendations and the rationale so we can size nodes and queues for Dedicated capacity.

High-level recommendation (multi-pool):
- Pool A (low-latency chat): pinned GPUs with strict concurrency limits and KV cache warmers. Target p95 tail: <=700ms.
- Pool B (re-rank & embeddings): mixed-occupancy nodes that can accept higher batching; lower priority preemptible slots for nightly batch re-ranks.
- Pool C (burst capacity): reserved but cold-scaled nodes that can be warmed via fast warm-start and short-lived instances for marketing spikes.

Autoscaling policy suggestions:
- Scale on effective tokens/sec per GPU and queue depth; prefer token-rate-based autoscaling for chat to avoid thrashing on short spikes.
- Minimums: keep 2 nodes available for Pool A (hot) to preserve tail latency during unexpected failures.
- Scale-up cooldown: 30s for added capacity; scale-down cooldown: 120s (to avoid churning during traffic noise).

Concurrency and queue sizing guidance (back-of-envelope):
- Chat pool: assume mean latency 120ms at concurrency 16 per GPU for your prompt distribution. For p95 target, cap per-GPU concurrency at 12 for chat models with KV cache.
- If peak chat QPS = 220 and avg tokens per request ~120, estimate tokens/sec = 220 * 120 / avg_generation_time. Using conservative generation_time 0.12s per token (model dependent) we size for ~880 tokens/sec per request — run sim with actual perf numbers.
- Queue depth: allow soft queue up to 4x concurrency per GPU (so clients see transient queueing vs immediate 429). Implement circuit-breaker where queue depth > 3x baseline triggers 429s for low-priority requests.

Routing & tenancy options:
- Per-customer queues: recommended for strict isolation; each customer gets reservation buckets and burst allowances. Adds management complexity but prevents noisy-neighbor issues.
- Shared multi-tenant pool with rate-limited per-route tokens is cheaper ops-wise but requires throttles and request prioritization (we can implement customer-weighted fair queuing).

Auth & SDK:
- For Private deployments, strongly recommend mTLS + OIDC for workload-to-workload; API keys OK for hosted with short rotation and key-scoped policies.
- SDK: include built-in retry with exponential backoff, jitter, and a 429/503 handler that respects Retry-After. Provide sample snippet (we’ll put this in the deep-dive):
  - Default client-side concurrency limit = 16 requests; allow override via config.
  - Enable streaming responses where possible to reduce client-side blocking for long generations.

Embeddings & re-rankers:
- Buffer embeddings requests in a small async queue to smooth spikes; use batched encoding for tokens to reduce GPU overhead.
- For re-rankers, prefer batched rerank pipelines with a prioritized queue to avoid starving chat traffic.

Open questions for sizing run:
- Exact model variants (e.g., 13B vs 70B) and measured tokens/sec for your typical prompts.
- Tail latency SLO for p99 — if you need p99 < 1s we’ll need larger warm pools and tighter concurrency caps.

Next step: I can run a quick node-count sim if you confirm models and paste per-route tokens/sec and P95 generation time. Recommend 60-min deep-dive tomorrow — I can bring perf numbers and a quick sim to show tradeoffs.
